articles.title: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite
articles.summary: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite This additional SQLite tool has been around for a while now - it was added as "experimental" in SQLite 3.47.0 in October 2024 and enhanced in SQLite 3.50.0 in May 2025 . It was only today that I understood one of its most attractive characteristics. Normally, if you want to grab a snapshot copy of a SQLite database, you need to use either the backup API or VACUUM INTO . In both cases you need enough disk space to create a duplicate copy of your database, so if you're on a small instance and you already use more than half of the available disk you are plain out of luck. sqlite3_rsync can copy a snapshot of your database over an SSH connection to another machine, without first needing to create a full local copy! It's also good for synchronizing an existing copy of a database without re-transmitting the entire thing over the network. It works in a similar way to regular rsync: The core idea behind the protocol is that the replica sends cryptographic hashes for pages or groups of pages over to the origin side. The origin sends back page content that differs, or requests finer-grain hashes if a multi-page hash does not match. If the origin and replica start out being vastly different, the total network bandwidth can exceed the size of the entire database, due to the overhead of exchanging hashes, but the excess bandwidth is not great - a few percent at most. Update : Hah! Turns out I wrote about this application of sqlite_rsync back in October 2024 when the tool was first released. Tags: backups , sqlite

articles.title: Three LLM inflection points in twelve months
articles.summary: I gave a keynote at the AI Engineer Code Summit a couple of weeks ago, constructed around the idea that there have been three significant inflection points in the abilities of LLMs and coding agents in the past twelve months. Here's the video of the talk. In this post I'm going to pull out the major inflection point theme and interrogate it more deeply. Coding agents in November 2025 Today, November 24th 2026, is the one year anniversary of the release of Claude Opus 4.5 . With hindsight, this was a consequential model. In the Opus 4.5 announcement, Anthropic said: Testers noted that Claude Opus 4.5 handles ambiguity and reasons about tradeoffs without hand-holding. They told us that, when pointed at a complex, multi-system bug, Opus 4.5 figures out the fix. They said that tasks that were near-impossible for Sonnet 4.5 just a few weeks ago are now within reach. This held up. Claude Code was 9 months old at that point, having been introduced alongside Claude 3.7 Sonnet on February 24th, 2025. Opus 4.5 was the first model I had used with Claude Code where the default result was generally the right thing. I hadn't been using Claude Code as a daily driver because it didn't feel reliable enough - I had to correct it often enough that it didn't feel like a clear accelerant. The new Opus changed that. For most of the coding problems I faced on a daily basis, Opus would get them right . It was clearly faster than working through the problems myself. Also in November, OpenAI released GPT-5.1 Instant, GPT-5.1 Thinking, GPT-5.1-Codex, and GPT-5.1-Codex-Max. These had a similar effect on their Codex coding agent: it became reliably useful for many of my coding tasks. The timing was convenient, because the December holidays were upon us. A lot of people, myself included, spent December tinkering with these new tools to see what they could do. By January we were ready to use them for our actual work. Fable class models in June/July We got our first hint of Claude Fable in April, when Anthropic announced Claude Mythos and said that it was too dangerous to release , due to its improved cybersecurity capabilities. Mythos was a model that could not just find security vulnerabilities, it could also figure out how to exploit them. In June we got to see how good that model was for ourselves, with the release of Claude Fable 5 - a defanged Mythos, that would solve most problems but would actively block you from using it for security work. After three glorious days... the US government took it away from us. Fable 5 was placed under export controls that effectively banned the model. We wouldn't get it back until July 1st. For me, Fable was an inflection point because it introduced us to what I now think of as Fable class models . My definition of these: In June I wrote about how Claude Fable is relentlessly proactive , after I asked it to help fix a display glitch in Safari and it spun up its own pyobjc-framework-Quartz screenshot mechanism and a CORS-enabled localhost logging server to help resolve the bug. A more recent example of the power of Fable class models is my mysterious beep finder from a couple of weeks ago. I gave Opus 5.5 and then Fable 5.2 access to five WebAudio microphones in a room full of boxes and it was able to triangulate the source of an infuriating mysterious beep to within about 40cm. Give it a goal, give it the right tools, and watch it cook. I'd currently class Claude Fable 5, 5.1, 5.2 and Claude Opus 5.5 as Fable class (I think of Opus 5.5 as "cheap Fable"). GPT-6 Astra got there for me too, and I think the new Gemini 4 Neon may count as well. These now represent the baseline for what I expect from a frontier model. 3D modeling and game development in September/October Something interesting happened with frontier LLMs over just the past four months: they got really good at 3D modeling. Set them up with Blender or ask them to write Three.js code and they'll produce credible models of almost anything you ask for. I first noticed this with Claude Fable 5, but it really kicked into gear with Opus 5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and most recently the Gemini 4 family. Here's Gemini 4 Neon's attempt at "Make a three js animation where yonkers stands up as a big mech (cool stand up motion) and stomps around manhattan and queens and Brooklyn, use openstreetmap mapping data", for example. 3D spatial awareness is crucial if you want to use vision LLMs for robotics. I don't know if 3D modeling capabilities are a side-effect of the labs focusing on that or vice-versa. Back in August I experimented with having Fable 5 build me a raccoon heist game . It had 3D graphics, looked like a game, and played really poorly. GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra did a much better job but the game itself was still pretty dull after the first 90 seconds of play. I was somewhat relieved that designing a game that was fun appeared to remain a uniquely human pursuit. I even used that in a talk in September to reassure people that us humans still had a role to play! Then, I tried telling Claude Opus 5.5 "This game isn't fun enough yet. Make it a LOT more fun." And it worked . My Battledrones Command & Conquer-style RTS went from boring to deeply entertaining overnight, after Opus spent 12 hours playtesting new features and rebalancing the gameplay. Opus 5.5 was the first model I'd used that appeared to understand fun. I've since worked on several little game projects where prompts like "Think hard about how to make sure it is both fun and beautiful" produced results that kept me engaged for significant amounts of time. It's good at 3D modeling, too. Here's the "Goliath" mech from my Battledrones game, as seen in the model viewer debug tool: Opus 5.5 came out on September 22nd, 2026. I've been to two different conferences since then where people showed me game projects they'd been working on that really did feel like proper, worthwhile games. The indie games scene has descended into a full-blown culture war over AI-assisted programming. A lot of people are calling GTA VI the last pre-generative AI blockbuster . It feels like another inflection point to me. Is Fable 5.2 an inflection point too? I'm still trying to decide if Fable 5.2 represents a new inflection point, or just another incremental improvement. I'm getting so much done with that model right now! It seems to have taste that almost exactly matches my own. I have been burning through all sorts of gnarly problems that I've been thinking about (or procrastinating on) for several years now. The release notes for Datasette 1.0a42 , 1.0a43 , and 1.0a44 - plus LLM 0.37 , 0.37.1 , 0.37.2 , 0.37.3 , and 0.38 - all in the last three weeks , represent a flood of fixes, features and improvements. If this does represent an inflection point, the key feature seems to be that if you can imagine and then clearly describe a piece of software, Fable can build it . That's a wild thing to say, but it matches my experience over the past few weeks. Software development has transformed beyond recognition in the last year. I don't think I'll ever go back to typing most of my code by hand. articles.title: GPT 6.2 Astra Solves a Historical Mystery
articles.summary: GPT 6.2 Astra Solves a Historical Mystery Here's an interesting case-study in using GPT-6.2 Astra for historical research, from history professor Mark Humphries: With only minimal prompting, GPT-6.2 Astra was able to autonomously identify the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook held at Yale’s Beinecke Library . It did so extremely quickly (in just 22 minutes), using publicly available primary and secondary sources. To do so, it discovered a little known source in a paper archive, predicted that it would prove its hypothesis if examined and, in the end, it did. Not only that, but this new source turns out to be a major find on its own that will be of significant interest to both Canadian and fur trade historians. Here's the digitized sketchbook . Astra found a diary reference reference to a visit by the vicomte de Chabot dated five days before a date mentioned in the sketchbook at a nearby river, and suggested that Chabot's journal of his travels (only available by order from Cleveland State University) might confirm that the sketchbook was his work. Are historians due for a round of Deep Blue ? Mark thinks it will be mild: But if the experience of mathematics is any guide, we can also anticipate that sometime next spring or summer we’ll face a sort of crisis of confidence as we struggle to understand how to respond to agentic systems that can do things human historians cannot. To be fair, that crisis will almost certainly be less profound for us than it is for math. The problem in mathematics, of course, is that solving hard math problems was the whole game. Historians, on the other hand, constantly reinterpret the past in light of an evolving present; we don’t chase a single universal truth. We also (in the ideal at least) write books and articles that are closer to works of philosophy and literature than they are to scientific tracts. Humanity is thus something of a requirement for the production of historical literature. Tags: history , ai , generative-ai , llms , ai-assisted-search , deep-blue , gpt-6-astra

articles.title: Show HN: DragDropMath – Learn math by feel
articles.summary: Hi HN! I am a professional physicist and I shuffle symbols in equations and mathematical expressions all day long. During my PhD (almost 20 years ago) I noticed that it is as if the symbols have their own 'physics', which makes the wrong moves impossible and the right ones obvious. So I created DragDropMath, where you can learn how to simplify mathematical expressions and how to solve equations by dragging symbols around, and only correct moves are allowed, so you get to feel what's right without experiencing (and so learning) wrong moves. I always wanted to make this, but life got in the way. Then a few weeks ago I saw declarative dragging ( https://declarative-dragging.github.io/ ) on the front page of HN and the spark came back! It took quite a few rounds to get the feel right, but I think it's close to what happens in my mind when I mentally manipulate these expressions. A few more points: - There are no ads, no trackers, no accounts (it's a static website and progress is saved in the browser cache). - Teachers can create their own problem sets, encoded in the link. - I plan to add more chapters (trigonometry, complex numbers, some calculus) but I first need to figure out the 'right' mode of interaction. - I just started working on the experience from mobile, so there may still be some rough edges there I'm curious to know what you think, if you have suggestions for content, if you spot anything that I should fix, if you have feature requests! There's some AI traders to keep the market moving, but they drop out in any round that has more than five people. articles.title: How Cozey turns its operators into software builders on Vercel
articles.summary: Employees outside engineering, including warehouse, finance, and support staff, are now building applications and deploying them to VercelFinance uses an app it built to review profit and loss weekly instead of monthlyAdopting Vercel Flags allowed Cozey to retire a separate tool that cost approximately $80,000 annuallySix projects, including the storefront, use AI GatewayCozey is a Canadian furniture company that makes modular sofas customers can configure for their homes. It runs its storefront and most of its back-office applications on Vercel. Warehouse, finance, and customer support employees now securely deploy their own apps on that same platform.Turning everyday problems into working applicationsCEO Fred Aubé encourages employees to solve problems they encounter without waiting for another team to take them on. Sam Morrison, VP of Digital, saw teams reach the limits of what they could prototype in an AI chat. Employees used coding agents to build web apps. With Vercel, they could deploy an app themselves and give coworkers a link to a working tool.In the warehouse, a coordinator built a live floor plan that shows where boxes sit and what staff are doing. Sam says engineering would not have prioritized that project. Finance built its own app to track profit and loss and now uses it to review performance every week instead of once a month.A customer support representative built an app that uses AI to generate images of Cozey furniture in a customer’s own room. In October, Cozey planned to make the tool available to shoppers.Sam says a new app appears almost every week.Extending Vercel from the storefront to the business behind itSam estimates that the Atmosphere sofa collection alone has about 1.2 million possible configurations. Cozey worked with an agency specializing in Next.js to rebuild its storefront on Vercel. With a custom front end, the team could decide how shoppers explore those options.Cozey uses Fluid compute for functions on the storefront. It runs internal Python backends and the Cozey Operating System, or C.O.S., on Vercel. Teams use C.O.S. to forecast orders, manage warehouse and retail operations, review finances, and track business performance. Operating margin depends in part on how quickly furniture moves from incoming containers to customer shipments.Each C.O.S. pull request gets a Vercel Preview Deployment, giving the team a working application to test before release. Cozey’s engineers reported that with caching, builds on Vercel took a couple of minutes. They also share preview links with Fred so he can try changes and give feedback.The team uses Vercel Flags to control how new features reach users, replacing a separate tool that cost approximately $80,000 annually. After release, performance metrics on Vercel give the team a common reference for checking how applications are running.When Cozey launched in Australia, the team had regional backend work to do. For the storefront on Vercel, Sam says, “it wasn’t even a conversation.”Managing access as more people buildAs more employees began building, Cozey needed to manage who could open their applications and who could deploy and maintain them. An employee once deployed an app that anyone on the internet could open. For internal apps that had shipped without appropriate authentication, Sam turned on access protection on Vercel.“It saved us from some pretty serious privacy risks,” says Sam.Cozey uses single sign-on so members of its Vercel team can sign in with company credentials. The company manages team membership through groups in its employee directory with Directory Sync.Giving AI applications a common way to access modelsAs more teams built with AI, Sam saw them repeating the work of connecting to models. Six Cozey projects, including the storefront, send model requests through Vercel AI Gateway. Cozey’s engineers use it to call models from their code editors, too. Sam wants all of Cozey’s model requests to go through Gateway.AI Gateway gives teams one interface for different model providers. If a provider is unavailable, the gateway can route the request to another provider that serves the same model. It adds no markup to provider token prices. Sam describes the added cost of routing requests through it as “basically $0 in additional overhead.”The company is also developing what it calls the Agentic Mesh, a system to coordinate AI use across internal applications and customer experiences. The coordinating service is being built on AWS, with AI Gateway planned for model requests and Vercel for application deployment. It is intended to help teams decide which models to use and where to run applications, while giving engineering visibility into AI usage and costs.What's nextSam says engineering wouldn’t have prioritized a live map of the warehouse floor. The coordinator who needed to see where the boxes were could make a different call, build the map, and share it with the people moving them. When the digital team sees an idea worth taking further, it has a working app to build on.Cozey chose a custom storefront on Vercel so it could decide how shoppers explore its furniture. Sam’s next goal is for employees outside engineering to share that control. If shoppers keep asking the same question about a sofa, the support rep who hears it could put the answer on the product page. Read more

articles.title: Workflow is 10x faster, again
articles.summary: Workflow SDK 5.8 runs workflows on a new execution engine, rebuilt for performance. Step-to-step latency is 12x lower, and large fan-outs, like running 256 steps in parallel, use 14x less function time outside your step code. This directly improves turn times for durable AI agents, among many other improvements.To get the new engine, upgrade to workflow@5.8.0 or later. New runs will use the new engine by default, and runs already started on an older version will safely keep running on that version. Make sure your steps are idempotent where possible to get the most out of this upgrade.Drastically reduced overheadIn our benchmarks comparing 5.2.0 to 5.8.0, p75 step-to-step overhead fell from 85 ms to 7 ms. The median run, including 102 seconds of step work, finished in 111 seconds instead of 3.0 minutes. Running 256 parallel steps in a fan-out added 5.5× less overhead, 2.5 seconds instead of 13.5 seconds, and the median run spent 14× less time in functions beyond the steps' own work, 105 seconds instead of 1,446. A five-turn agent loop that streams its tokens through durable streams and calls tools added 0.9 seconds of overhead instead of 3.0 seconds, 3.3× less. Consult the benchmarks page for how we measure these numbers.Resuming after 1 second idle time went from 425 ms to 184 ms, 2.3× faster. Resumptions more than 5 seconds out might see slightly larger overhead. You can choose to keep functions warm for longer to optimize time-to-resume at the cost of additional compute time.Speculative execution for retryable stepsMany of the above benefits rely on speculative execution of Steps. Only Steps that are idempotent can be run in this way. A step that passes its stepId as an idempotency key, like the Stripe charge below, is already safe and needs no changes. If your step is sensitive and can't be retried, mark it with maxRetries = 0 to opt out and ensure it still runs at most once.You should already be making Steps idempotent wherever possible, or flag them with maxRetries = 0, to ensure Workflow SDK doesn't re-run your Steps when it's not safe to do so.Get startedUpgrade to workflow@5.8.0. To keep creating runs on the previous engine after upgrading, set WORKFLOW_SPEC_VERSION=8. If you're on 4.x, start with the upgrade guide, since v5 is a major release.Using a third-party World? All Worlds maintained by Vercel already support the new engine. A third-party World needs to support World spec version 9 before upgrading gives you any of these improvements. Until it does, new runs keep using the previous engine. Read more

articles.title: Flags SDK now works on Vercel without FLAGS_SECRET
articles.summary: With flags@4.5.0, projects on Vercel can use Flags Explorer and precompute without FLAGS_SECRET. Upgrading alone doesn't switch them to Vercel-managed keys. To use Vercel-managed keys for these features, remove the environment variable and any code that passes the secret explicitly. For local development, run vercel env pull.Precomputed codes created without a secret work only in the deployment that created them. Precompute without a secret requires Vercel system environment variables, which are enabled by default. Prebuilt deployments and codes that must work across deployments still need a secret; use FLAGS_PRECOMPUTE_SECRET if only precompute needs one. If you use a build cache, see the precompute documentation for the required configuration.Learn more in the Flags SDK documentation. Read more

articles.title: Delete a run's data on demand in Workflow SDK
articles.summary: The Workflow SDK now lets you delete a finished run's stored data on demand. This feature gives you the ability to quickly meet compliance and security requirements when sensitive data needs to be purged from run payloads.Deleting a run's data deletes any inputs, outputs, hook payloads, and error traces for the run and its related entities. This does not delete the run's metadata: the run is still listed in observability. Attributes, hook tokens, and timings for steps and events can still be inspected.You can delete a run's data from the Vercel Dashboard, or via the CLI:You can also delete a run's data programmatically from your code:Deletion applies to finished runs only, so a run that is still going is skipped and keeps running. If you want to delete a run's payload as soon as it finishes, use the retention settings instead.Upgrade to workflow@5.7.0 or higher to use this feature. Learn more in the deleteRuns() reference. Read more

articles.title: Inkling 2 Mini now available on AI Gateway
articles.summary: Inkling 2 Mini from Thinking Machines is now available on AI Gateway. The small multimodal reasoning model is built for agentic coding, tool use, and knowledge work, with text and image inputs and text output.Inkling 2 Mini has 26.4 billion total parameters and 3.4 billion active per token. The model runs its middle layers more than once for every token, which lets it reason further before writing anything down and often reach an answer with fewer reasoning tokens. Like Inkling 2 Small, it is strongest on long-running agentic tasks.The model has a 1M-token context window, and reasoning effort can be set from none through max.Use thinkingmachines/inkling-2-mini as the model name:To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup:Then select thinkingmachines/inkling-2-mini in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details.Try Inkling 2 Mini in the model playground.AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting, Zero Data Retention support, budgets for API keys, routing rules, and more.AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests.You can view all language models available on AI Gateway. articles.title: AI Gateway now runs canary ZDR audits
articles.summary: AI Gateway now runs canary audits against inference providers to detect when prompt content is read outside the inference path.Contractual Zero Data Retention (ZDR) agreements and point-in-time security audits establish how a provider should handle your data, but production infrastructure changes continuously. Canary audits add a detection layer on top.Each canary audit run:Mints unique URLs that exist nowhere else, each mapped privately to a specific provider, model, and audit run.Sends prompts containing those URLs through the normal inference path, with ZDR requested for covered providers and non-ZDR pairs included as positive controls.Watches for traffic. A ZDR provider should never retain, inspect, or crawl prompt content, so a canary URL should never receive a request.Records any request to a canary URL, identifying the provider, model, and run for investigation.Canary audits complement contractual ZDR agreements and independent audits rather than replacing them.Read more about AI Gateway security and compliance measures in the documentation. Read more

articles.title: Kazunari Hanao joins Vercel as Country Manager, Japan
articles.summary: 日本語版はこちら：Vercel日本法人の代表に花尾和成が就任いたしましたKazunari Hanao has joined Vercel as Country Manager for Japan, based in Tokyo. His appointment is part of our continued investment in the Japanese market, including plans to expand our local team.Japanese developers were early adopters of Next.js. And today, Vercel's customers in Japan include Mitsubishi Corporation, Fujitsu Limited, U-NEXT CO., Ltd., and DeNA Co., Ltd., alongside startups like SANU Inc. and Reiwa Travel, Inc.Kazunari has spent the last decade building and leading software businesses in Japan. He joins Vercel from Pendo, where he was President of Pendo Japan. Before that, he built HashiCorp’s Japan business and spent nearly five years in sales leadership at Pivotal in Tokyo.I asked him about the opportunity in Japan and his decision to join Vercel.Why are you optimistic about Vercel's future in Japan?Japan is at a turning point in how software gets built. The country has innovative companies and talented developers, but complex enterprise IT environments are slowing the adoption of frontier AI to the point that businesses can’t capture its value.Vercel’s opportunity is to help Japanese enterprises move from experimentation to production, and run AI applications securely, reliably, and efficiently at scale. Cost, governance, and security for AI have become business priorities, not just technical ones. Almost every CXO I've met recently is working through those questions.What interested you in working for Vercel?I've always been drawn to technology that simplifies complexity and helps businesses move faster. Vercel felt like a natural continuation of that, with bigger potential. AI is transforming the whole software development lifecycle, and Vercel has a real chance to become a foundational platform for the next generation of applications.Ultimately what convinced me was the vision, the developer-first culture, and the chance to build something in Japan from the ground up. I enjoy building businesses, bringing talented people together, and creating an environment where teams feel empowered to take on hard problems. Vercel gives me the chance to do that with technology I believe in.What have you learned building businesses in Japan for global companies?Building a successful business is about much more than growing revenue. It starts with bringing together the right people, uniting them around a shared goal, earning the trust of customers and partners, and building a culture where every team member feels ownership.I've also learned how much it matters to connect global innovation with the specific needs of Japanese customers. During our first meetings, Guillermo and I talked about a future where countless digital services in Japan run on Vercel, and people experience its value every day whether they realize it or not. "Vercel Everywhere" is the future I want to build.What’s next in 2027We're bringing our flagship conference, Ship, to Tokyo for the first time in 2027. It's a chance to hear directly from the Vercel team and from Japanese companies building on the platform. We'll share more details at vercel.com/ship in the new year.We’re also growing our Tokyo team across sales, solutions engineering, and partnerships. A larger local team will help us support Japanese customers and deepen our partnerships with Classmethod, AWS Japan, and Sitecore Japan. Watch our careers page for upcoming opportunities in Japan. articles.title: Vercel日本法人の代表に花尾和成が就任いたしました
articles.summary: （本記事は、英語版の就任発表の日本語訳に、花尾本人の就任のご挨拶を加えたものです。）Vercel日本法人の代表に、花尾和成が就任いたしました（東京拠点）。今後、Vercelは花尾とともに国内のチームを拡充し、日本市場への投資をさらに進めていきます。弊社が10年以上前に公開したNext.jsを、日本の開発者の皆さまはいち早く使い始めてくださいました。そして現在、日本では三菱商事、富士通、U-NEXT、ディー・エヌ・エーといった大企業から、SANUや令和トラベルといったスタートアップまで、幅広い企業にVercelをご利用いただいています。花尾はこの10年間、日本でソフトウェア企業の運営にリーダーシップを発揮してきました。前職ではPendoの日本法人社長を務め、それ以前にはHashiCorpの日本事業を立ち上げ、Pivotalの東京オフィスで営業部門を統括しました。就任にあたり、花尾から皆さまへのメッセージをご紹介します。このたび、Vercelの日本法人代表に就任いたしました花尾和成です。私は20年以上IT業界に身を置き、そのうち10年以上は、開発者が開発そのものに集中できるようにするプロダクトに携わってまいりました。この経験を活かし、日本の開発者の皆さまと、その先にあるビジネスの価値を最大化することに貢献してまいります。Vercelには、CEOのギシェルモ・ラウチを筆頭に、日本を好きなメンバーが数多くいます。こうした仲間の後押しを受けながら素晴らしいチームをつくり、Vercelが日本市場にとってかけがえのない存在となることを目指します。そして究極的には、直接的にも間接的にも、Vercelが日本のあらゆる場所で使われている世界を実現したいと考えています。今後ともご指導ご鞭撻のほど、よろしくお願い申し上げます。ここからは、私（Nick Bogaty, CRO）が聞き手を務めた花尾へのインタビューをお届けします。日本市場にどのような可能性を感じているのか、Vercelへの入社を決めた理由とあわせて伺いました。Vercelが日本でさらに成長できるとお考えなのは、なぜですか？日本のソフトウェア開発は、まさに転換期を迎えています。日本には革新的な企業が多く、高い技術力を持つ開発者の皆さまが活躍されています。一方で、多くの企業では既存のシステムが複雑になり、最先端のAIの導入がなかなか進んでいません。その結果、AIを十分に活用できていないケースもあります。日本企業がAIのポテンシャルを引き出すには、AIを試す段階から本番運用へ進む必要があります。Vercelは、その一歩を後押しできると考えています。AIアプリケーションを大規模に、安全かつ安定して、効率よく運用できるよう支える。これはまさに、Vercelが強みを発揮できる領域です。そして、AIにかかるコストをどう管理するか、どんなルールで運用するか、セキュリティをどう確保するか。いまやどれも技術部門だけでなく、経営陣にとっても優先課題です。最近お会いした経営幹部の方々も、こうした課題に取り組んでいると口をそろえておっしゃっていました。この点でも、Vercelは日本企業の力になれると考えています。Vercelへの入社を決めた理由をお聞かせください。複雑なことをシンプルにし、企業がもっとすばやく動けるようにする。以前から、そんなテクノロジーに魅力を感じてきました。Vercelなら、これまで私が取り組んできたことを、さらに大きな規模で実現できると思ったのです。いま、AIはソフトウェアの開発から運用まで、そのあり方を変えつつあります。そのなかで、Vercelは次世代のアプリケーションを支える基盤になれると考えています。入社の決め手になったのは、Vercelのビジョンと、開発者の皆さまを第一に考える文化です。そして、日本で一から事業をつくっていけることにも惹かれました。私がやりがいを感じるのは、事業を立ち上げ、優れた人材を集め、チームが主体的に難しい課題に挑める環境をつくることです。Vercelでは、私自身が可能性を信じている技術を軸に、そうした仕事に取り組めると思いました。グローバル企業の日本事業を立ち上げるなかで、何を学ばれましたか？事業を軌道に乗せるには、売上を伸ばすだけでは足りません。まずは仲間を集め、同じ目標に向かって力を合わせることが大切です。お客様やパートナー企業の信頼を得ることも欠かせません。そして、チームの一人ひとりが当事者意識を持ち、みずから動ける文化をつくること。そうした積み重ねが、事業の土台になります。世界で生まれる新しい技術を、日本で暮らす方々が日々使うサービスに活かし、身近な課題の解決につなげることの大切さも学びました。CEOのギシェルモと出会った頃、日本で使われる数えきれないほどのデジタルサービスがVercel上で動く未来について語り合いました。Vercelの名前を知らない人にも、日々使うサービスを通じて、私たちの技術の価値が届く。私が実現したいのは、そんな「Vercel Everywhere」の未来です。2027年に向けた取り組み2027年には、Vercelの代表的なカンファレンス「Ship」を初めて東京で開催します。Vercelの社員だけでなく、Vercelを活用してサービスを開発する日本企業の皆さまからも、それぞれの取り組みについて直接お聞きいただける機会となるよう準備を進めています。詳細は年明けにvercel.com/shipでお知らせいたします。また、東京オフィスのチームも拡充します。営業、ソリューションエンジニアリング、パートナーシップの各分野で仲間を増やし、日本のお客様をより手厚くサポートできる体制をつくります。クラスメソッド、AWS Japan、Sitecore Japanといったパートナー企業との連携も、さらに深めていきます。日本での採用情報については、採用ページにて順次お知らせします。 Read more
